historical_basis: According to Swedish legend, the Knights of Ålleberg are the ghosts of twelve knights killed at the Battle of Åsle in 1389; the legend exemplifies the king-asleep-in-the-mountain motif. The story has the ghosts trapped in Ålleberg mountain, awaiting a new war to wake them to fight for the country; the mountain is also thought to host trolls. The commonest legend tells of a farmer taking grain to market in Falköping; a man asked to buy the whole load, and the farmer followed him into a hall in the mountain where the knights slept in full armour. The farmer happened to knock a bridle so it jingled, and the riders woke asking whether it was time; the man who had bought the load assured them they could sleep on.
